review_notes: Reviewed the whole file (134 lines), including `basisAux`, `basis`, the base-change basis lemmas, `instFree`, `toMatrix_baseChange`, and their verification and use sites. Inspected the generic base-change basis interface in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Basis.lean (`baseChange_repr_tmul`, `baseChange_apply`), the `Basis.repr`/`repr_symm` simp lemmas in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Basis/Defs.lean and the `Finsupp.linearCombination` simp lemmas, the `Finsupp.mapRange` interface (Mathlib/Data/Finsupp/Defs.lean, Mathlib/Data/Finsupp/SMulWithZero.lean), `Matrix.map_apply`/`LinearMap.toMatrix_apply`, and the uses in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Trace.lean, Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/Polynomial.lean and Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Charpoly/BaseChange.lean. I deliberately did not report the non-pointwise right-hand side of `basis_repr_tmul` (the pointwise form is reached via the simp lemma `Finsupp.mapRange_apply`), the `@[simp]` tag on `toMatrix_baseChange` (the `Matrix.map` form is exactly what Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/Polynomial.lean consumes), or the un-tagged `basis_repr_symm_apply`/`basis_repr_symm_apply'` (the `repr.symm`/`linearCombination` simp chain already derives the tensor form). Uncertainty: whether the `basisAux`/`basis` structure-update makes the tagged `basis_repr_tmul` strictly reusable for `basisAux` goals; the proposed change makes the auxiliary interface self-sufficient anyway.

theorem basisAux_tmul (a : A) (m : M) :
    basisAux A b (a ⊗ₜ m) = a • Finsupp.mapRange (algebraMap R A) (map_zero _) (b.repr m) := by
findings.problem: `basisAux_tmul` is the evaluation lemma for the publicly defined auxiliary linear equivalence `basisAux` (`A ⊗[R] M ≃ₗ[R] ι →₀ A`), and its right-hand side is the same canonical normal form as the `@[simp]` lemma `basis_repr_tmul` (lines 68-71), but it carries no `@[simp]` attribute. Consequently, when a goal mentions `basisAux` rather than the `A`-linear `basis`, the rewrite must be supplied by hand: line 60 uses `simp only [TensorProduct.smul_tmul', basisAux_tmul, smul_assoc]`, and line 75 unfolds with `simp [basis, Equiv.uniqueProd_symm_apply, basisAux]`. The simp interface therefore covers `(basis A b).repr` but not the `R`-linear map that users of `basisAux` actually see.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to `basisAux_tmul`, keeping its current statement and its `basisAux ... (a ⊗ₜ m)` left-hand side, so that it sits next to `basis_repr_tmul` with the same right-hand side. This introduces no new normal form: the right-hand side is identical to the one already chosen by the `@[simp]` lemma `basis_repr_tmul`, and it contains no `basisAux` applied to a tensor, so it cannot create a rewrite cycle with `TensorProduct.smul_tmul'` or `Finsupp.mapRange_apply`. The explicit `simp only` list at line 60 may keep mentioning it, but it would no longer be required.
findings.benefit: A user whose goal involves `basisAux A b (a ⊗ₜ m)` (for instance because the `R`-linear structure is what is in scope, as in the `basisAux_map_smul` proof) obtains the evaluation by plain `simp`, consistently with the already-simplifying `basis_repr_tmul`. The public simp interfaces of the two related maps (`basisAux` and `basis`) then match, and manual lemma lists in this file get shorter.
